::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 23d [1872]  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels[^1]
:::

My dear [Christabel](people/person_329.qmd)
Here is the pay for [Minne’s Knight](other_books/otherbook_818.qmd), with many thanks.[^2]  I conclude you are at home.  You will see proposals for a monstrous Goose affair in the next packet, but I shall get help in the selection of the essays.[^3]  I hope you will do the Snow and Sun next year

Who asks our question next?  I should think [Hanbury Mills](other_books/otherbook_829.qmd) must be a great success, every body seems to like it who has read it  I am much afraid the Awdry’s departure will be the ruin of our [lectures](organizations/other_240.qmd), there seems to be no one to take the same pains about them[^4]

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The paper has a decorated motif  ‘New Year’s Day With the Season’s Cheer and a Friend’s Regards.'
[^2]: ‘Minne’s Knight’ was Coleridge's contribution to the *MP* Christmas number of 1872..
[^3]: *MP* (January 1873) carries on the back an advertisement for ['COBWEBS OR, THE MONTHLY PACKET ESSAY SOCIETY](organizations/other_116.qmd).  *Two Questions, to be Answered in Writing, on History, Literature, Art or Science, will be proposed in each Number.  Answers to be directed to* ARACHNE, CARE OF THE EDITOR OF THE MONTHLY PACKET.'
[^4]: The Rev.[William Awdry](people/person_85.qmd) (1842-1910) and his wife since 1868, former Gosling Frances [Emily Moberly](people/person_81.qmd) (1844-1921) had been the moving spirits in bringing lecturers to Winchester in connection with the movement for the higher education of women.
